content.value_statement: Azure Service Bus applications need reliable patterns for messaging, settlement, sessions, and operations. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused .NET SDK guidance.
actual_capabilities: Shows package installation for Azure.Messaging.ServiceBus and Azure.Identity.
Explains authentication with DefaultAzureCredential and connection strings.
Provides examples for sending, receiving, batching, and settling messages.
Covers processors, sessions, dead-letter queues, topics, and subscriptions.
Includes administration examples for queues, topics, and subscriptions.
Summarizes SDK types, error handling, and operational best practices.
limitations: Does not validate live Azure resources, permissions, or namespace settings.
Does not replace testing under production load or failure conditions.
Focuses on the .NET SDK and does not cover other language SDKs.
SDK versions and Azure service behavior can change after publication.

use_cases.title: Create Queue-Based Messaging
use_cases.description: Design send and receive flows with message completion, batching, and safe settlement behavior.

use_cases.title: Add Ordered Processing
use_cases.description: Use sessions and session receivers when a workflow needs ordered processing per business key.

use_cases.title: Operate Messaging Entities
use_cases.description: Review administration patterns for creating, updating, and deleting Service Bus queues, topics, and subscriptions.

prompt_templates.title: Start With Service Bus
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add Azure Service Bus to a .NET application. Show the packages, authentication choice, and a simple queue send and receive flow.

prompt_templates.title: Design Message Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a .NET Service Bus consumer for my queue. Include message completion, abandon behavior, batching, and error handling guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Use Sessions and Topics
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a .NET Service Bus design using topics, subscriptions, and sessions. Explain when to use each feature and what code patterns matter.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Azure Service Bus .NET implementation for production readiness. Focus on credentials, lock duration, retries, dead letters, and transactions.

output_examples.input: I need a simple .NET queue sender and receiver.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan covering packages, DefaultAzureCredential, sender creation, receiver creation, message completion, and disposal order.

output_examples.input: My messages must stay ordered per order ID.
output_examples.output: A session-based design that explains session IDs, session receivers, session state, lock renewal, and where ordering guarantees apply.

output_examples.input: I need to handle failed messages safely.
output_examples.output: A processing checklist covering manual completion, abandon behavior, dead-letter reasons, retry decisions, and dead-letter queue inspection.

best_practices: Prefer DefaultAzureCredential for production authentication when the environment supports managed identity.
Use processors for background workers because they simplify concurrency and lock renewal.
Create batches with TryAddMessage so oversized messages are handled before sending.
anti_patterns: Do not complete a message before the business operation has succeeded.
Do not create a new ServiceBusClient for every message or request.
Do not rely on connection strings in production when managed identity is available.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation and examples. Users decide whether to run package installation or application code.

faq.question: Which .NET package does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Azure.Messaging.ServiceBus and includes Azure.Identity for Microsoft Entra ID authentication.

faq.question: Can it help with queues and topics?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers queue senders and receivers, topic senders, and subscription receivers.

faq.question: Does it cover ordered message processing?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Service Bus sessions, session receivers, session state, and lock renewal.

faq.question: Can it manage Service Bus entities?
faq.answer: It includes examples for ServiceBusAdministrationClient to create, update, and delete queues, topics, and subscriptions.

faq.question: Is it a substitute for Azure testing?
faq.answer: No. You still need to test credentials, permissions, throughput, retries, and failure handling in your Azure environment.
